newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold Q3 net profit seen up 55 percent.
newsitem.headline: Ahold Q3 net profit seen up 55 percent.

text.p: Net profit at Dutch supermarkets group Ahold is expected to surge 55 percent in the third quarter of 1996, boosted by the consolidation chain Stop & Shop, analysts said on Friday.
They expect Ahold to post a 1996 third quarter net profit of between 134 and 170 million guilders, with a consensus of 158 million, up from 10llion in the same period last year.
"Stop & Shop will be the main item, the rest will be business as usual, showing a continuation of the trends of the first half," said ING Barings' analyst Dennis Jullens.
Analysts said it was difficult to estimate the exact contribution of Stop & Shop, included in Ahold's resultfirst time. Ahold acquired it in July for $2.9 billion.
Their estimates varied from a 30 million guilder contribution to net profit, to a $65 million contribution to the operating result.
"It is a bit of a guess, as we don't know much about the seasonal influences," said Corne Zandbergen from Generale Bank.
Stop & Shop 1995 annual sales were $4.1 billion, while Ahold USA totalled $8.3 billion sales in 1995.
Stop & Shop made several acquisitions since the third quarter of last year, complicating comparisons.
The obligatory closure of 35 Edward stores will pressure profit growth in the U.S., analysts said, but operating margins are seen rising.
"Stop & Shop has a 5.5 percent margin, and we expect the margin for the U.S. as a whole to rise to 3.3 percent (against 2.6 pct)," said Bangert's Paul Schram.
European activities other than in the Netherlands are seen continuing their second quarter expansion, when operating results rose nearly 33 percent.
"Czech activities have turnedEurope will rise to 6.7 percent, compared to six percent last year," said Schram.
Ahold's Dutch operating results are expected to continue their annual increase of around 10 percent.
"Apparently, there's still enough space for continuous improvement," said ING Baring's Jullens.
Schram said he expected Ahold's margin on Dutch activities to improve 10 basis points to 3.3 percent.
"Dutch margin improvement will slow down somewhat, pressured by integration of the Primarkt group, as it did in the second quarter," he said.
Supermarket and liquor chain Primarkt was acquired in January this year and Schram said he expected it to be fully integrated within a year, after which Dutch margins would improve more quickly.

Analysts did not think the rise of the dollar would have a big impact. "That will only amount to a couple of millions," said Generale Bank's Zandbergen. Last year, Ahold applied a dollar rate of 1.61 guilders during the third quarter.
On the whole, analysts were upbeat about Ahold's longer-term prospects.
"They are smart to invest in growth markets through joint-ventures with local players," said Zandbergen.
Analysts agreed it would take at least a year for Ahold's South-East Asian activities to contribute to profits, but that prospects were very good.

The Brazilian joint-venture announced at the beginning of this month also received a warm welcome from analysts. Ahold will enter a 50-50 joint venture with Brazilian retailer Bompreco, the fourth largest food retailer in the country. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
